newsitem.title: HAITI: Senator shot, officer killed in Haiti violence.
newsitem.headline: Senator shot, officer killed in Haiti violence.

text.p: A Haitian senator was shot and a police officer killed in separate incidents in a growing wave of violence in the Haitian capital, authorities said on Wednesday.
Sen. Mehu Garcon, 47, was shot four times on Tuesday evening and the driver off his car was killed when gunmen opened fire on his car on a highway in Port-au-Prince.
"It is with great luck that I am still alive. God alone saved me," Garcon, who represents Cap Haitien in northern Haiti, told Reuters from his hospital bed on Wednesday.
Three men surrounded his vehicle and opened fire, the senator said. The driver, Gary Aubas, was shot 12 times and died immediatly, according to Garcon.

"When I saw them shooting I ducked, that's what saved me. I have no idea who did it or why," Garcon said, adding that the attackers pulled him out and took the car. Doctors said Garcon was in stable condition.
Haitian police officer Franz Francois was shot and killed on Tuesday by gang members in Cite Soleil, according to Felder Jean-Baptiste, spokesman for the Haitian Naitonal Police.
The sprawling Port-au-Prince slum has been stricken by gang warfare in the past month. At least 11 residents have been killed and up to 100 houses burned in the conflict.
Radio Metropole reported three other police officers were killed around the capital on Tuesday, but police could not confirm those deaths.
Thirty-two people, including five police officers, have been killed in violence in the capital during the past two weeks, according to the newspaper Nouvelliste.
On Monday, the security chief for the Justice Ministry, Charles Avrinel, was shot to death by two men on a motorcycle.

"Many police, as well as citizens, have died by bullets recently," Senate president Edgar LeBlanc said at Garcon's bedside. "We don't know if it's a reaction to the conditions of the country or if it is an organised political campaign to destablize the government, but we must mobilise to keep it from increasing."

Edwin Stephen, who is running as an independent candidate for a senate seat in Cap Haitien in April 6 elections, said in a telephone interview that Garcon's shooting had provoked street protests and tire burning.
